ask: rig.rest topology amendment: agents run online, results store locally, online progress clearable
statement: AMENDS F-9. New topology: portal + CONNECTOR ONBOARDING on the web (the app asks for model connectors and sets up the rig); agents EXECUTE ONLINE (vendor sandboxes); results/estate STORE LOCALLY on the device; the user can CLEAR online progress at will. Positioning: we are just a harness — BYO models, the user owns the data, we sell neither. HONESTY CONSTRAINT (mentor, binding on all product copy): with online execution the working material DOES transit and reside temporarily in vendor compute, so the claim is NOT never-touches-the-cloud; the defensible claim is NOTHING PERSISTS ON OUR SIDE — ephemeral vendor compute, durable local storage, user-triggered purge with a RECEIPT (a purge that cannot be shown is an assertion, and this estate does not ship assertions). Differentiation ruled first-class, not decoration: the zero-token visual toolsets (river, journey, graph, cockpit) are the product identity — do the same work differently, more legibly, more visually.

ask: what did the owner actually ask for — online execution, or work that survives them leaving?
statement: NARROWS F-14 (mentor scope-inflation, owned): the owner clarified they wanted ONE capability — agents keep running when the portal or machine closes, and the user picks them back up when needed. That is a FEATURE (detachable, resumable work) not an ARCHITECTURE (everything executes online). It is already built and proven: beam (checkpoint to a pushed ref, respawn in cloud, recall home with DELIVERED/MISSING accounting) plus the verified rail physics (Anthropic cloud sessions persist with the browser closed; reclaimed environments restore history on reopen). RULED: default execution stays LOCAL per F-9; the cloud is an OPT-IN DEPARTURE PATH the user takes when they leave. What survives from F-14: connector onboarding as the front door, storage local, and — only where something WAS sent to the cloud — the purge receipt and the four residue classes, which shrink from an architecture-wide obligation to a per-departure one. Complexity removed on purpose: no results buffer question, no always-online residue, no parity copy problem.
